newsitem.title: INDIA: Four die, 20 missing after India ship sinks.
newsitem.headline: Four die, 20 missing after India ship sinks.

text.p: - Four crewmen died and 20 were missing after a ship sank off India's west coast on Thursday, the same day as another ship sank in a river near the eastern city of Calcutta.
"The ship has sunk completely due to a cyclone," a senior official of the Bombay Port Trust told Reuters. "It was called the M.V. Arcadia Pride, a cargo vessel with a deadweight of 13,672 tonnes."
Naval helicopters and coast guard ships searched for the 20 missing crew members, a defence spokesman told Reuters.
"We rescued 13 people, of whom four died soon after being taken to hospital," the spokesman said. "We're looking for about 20 more people."
Earlier on Thursday, the Panama-flagged cargo ship M.V. Green Opal, carrying 70,000 tonnes of steel, sank in a river near Calcutta, police and local news agencies said.
Police official K.K. Kalia told Reuters in Calcutta that the ship, on its way to Hong Kong, sank in the Hooghly river about 40 km (25 miles) from Calcutta.
"We know some crew members were rescued but details are awaited," Kalia said. Local news agencies said all 20 crew were rescued.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said the ship sank after hitting a barge. It quoted Calcutta Port Trust officials as saying the captain, the chief officer and the second officer were Korean and the remaining crew members were Filipinos.
The M.V. Arcadia Pride was carring sulphur to Bombay, the government said in a statement.
Officials of the firm that owns the vessel, Arcadia Shipping Pvt. Ltd, were not immediately available for comment.
